passage: Class 5 teacher's note, results day. Kavitha topped the class in the term exams and glowed all morning; twice I heard her tell the row in front what her total was. Then she noticed Ayesha folding a paper into a small square, and Kavitha stopped mid-sentence. At lunch she asked Ayesha to show her how to shade maps so neatly, and admitted her own map marks were her lowest. When I congratulated her, I said there was nothing wrong with feeling glad. She answered, "I'm really happy, but I don't want to be loud about it." I will see how she handles the next round of results. 🙂

qa.q: How many times did the teacher hear Kavitha tell the row in front what her total was?
qa.a: Twice; the teacher heard her tell the row in front what her total was.

qa.q: What was Kavitha feeling when she noticed Ayesha folding the paper, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Pride mixed with sudden thoughtfulness: she stopped mid-sentence and then asked Ayesha for help, saying she was happy but did not want to be loud.

qa.q: What would you advise Kavitha to do the next time results come out?
qa.a: Enjoy being glad, share the news quietly, and keep remembering what classmates like Ayesha are good at.

qa.q: How might Ayesha have felt when Kavitha asked for help with the maps?
qa.a: Ayesha may have felt noticed for a real strength after a disappointing morning, though it could also have stung a little; the note does not say.

grounding: Illustrates a top scorer feeling proud and choosing modest sharing while valuing a friend's strength.
